 FBI Miami searches for Colombian fugitive in $54M drug-money laundering operation 
 Investigators say Victor Julian Duque worked as a courier, collecting cash in the U.S. and depositing hundreds of thousands of dollars into accounts tied to fake businesses on behalf of the criminal organization Clan de Golfo. 
 By Briana Trujillo and NBC6 • 
 Published October 27, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 27, 2026 at 8:18 am 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Victor Julian Duque allegedly worked as the courrier collecting the cash in the United States, then depositing hundreds of thousands of dollars into accounts tied to fake businesses.
 The FBI is looking for a Colombian man accused of taking part in a massive drug-money laundering operation.
 Investigators say Victor Julian Duque (who may also go by Victor Julian Duque Tobon), worked as a courier, collecting cash in the U.S. and depositing hundreds of thousands of dollars into accounts tied to fake businesses on behalf of the criminal organization Clan de Golfo. 
 Watch NBC6 free wherever you are
   WATCH HERE 
 Since 2021, the organization he worked for "has allegedly laundered more than $54 million from fictitious businesses operating in the United States to businesses in Colombia," the FBI said. 
 Duque is accused of depositing a total of $459,953 between Sept. 26, 2022 and March 24, 2023. A federal arrest warrant was issued for him on Oct. 22, 2025 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida in Miami after he was charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering.
 Nine people have been indicted in connection with the investigation, officials said. 
 "Of the eight individuals arrested, six have been convicted," according to the FBI. 
 Duque is the only remaining fugitive in the case, and the FBI is offering up to $10,000 for information leading to his arrest.

 He is believed to be in Colombia and has ties to Pereira, Bogotá, and Belén, Colombia, as well as San Antonio, Texas.
 The FBI urges anyone with information about Duque’s whereabouts to contact their local FBI office, the nearest U.S. Embassy or Consulate, or submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov.
